A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DART work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Material can be matched reliably, including v1's Appendix D analyses that move into v2's main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original DART accuracy and latency measurements, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, cross-model evaluations, and token-interpretability results. Some baseline scores are explicitly attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds training-resource measurements, logic and commonsense evaluations, and a Llama-3.2-3B experiment.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same dual pathways, REM architecture, hidden-state distillation objective, 20 ST tokens, loss weight of 20, and ST-only inference. Evaluating additional models and tasks does not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v1's task coverage is arithmetic reasoning through GSM8K, GSM-HARD, SVAMP, and MultiArith. v2 retains these and adds fine-tuning and evaluation on ProsQA logical reasoning and CommonsenseQA-CoT commonsense reasoning, substantially broadening the represented task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CoT, Coconut, CODI, No-CoT, iCoT, and PauseFT. The cross-model comparison retains No-CoT, while the added task and resource comparisons use the already included CoT and No-CoT methods. No comparator is added or removed within a matched existing experiment.

E3.justification: v2 adds a Llama-3.2-3B condition with a 5e-4 learning rate and introduces total FLOPs and peak GPU memory as training-resource metrics. Existing arithmetic preprocessing, accuracy/latency evaluation, and reported training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds training-cost analysis and extends the cross-model robustness check to Llama-3.2-3B. The ST-count sensitivity experiment, component and alignment-token ablations, and decoded-token analysis already appear in v1; their relocation and consolidation are not new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's averaging of peak memory across eight GPUs defines a resource summary rather than introducing run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports DART accuracies of 99.4% on ProsQA and 75.1% on CommonsenseQA-CoT, versus CoT's 98.8% and 68.5%. Table 5 adds Llama-3.2-3B results: DART 46.6% versus No-CoT 40.8%, both at 62 ms. Table 2 adds training FLOPs and memory results. Matched arithmetic, ablation, sensitivity, GPT2/Qwen, and interpretability results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Section 3, shift-value derivation in Appendix A, and notation definitions are unchanged apart from table renumbering. No new assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections appear.

C1.justification: The abstract changes its headline claim from comparable performance to existing baselines with efficiency gains to performance gains over non-autoregressive baselines without extra inference latency. This refines the comparator scope and claimed advantage; the central DART contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning training and parameter efficiency, applicability across reasoning domains, and scalability to larger models. The existing ST-mechanism explanations and the three limitations concerning training resources, supervision, and CoT-data dependence are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses use of eight Nvidia A10 GPUs, absolute trainable-parameter counts, Llama-3.2-3B settings, and sample counts/examples for the added datasets. Appendix C explains the existing loss weight of 20. GPT2 and Qwen training settings move from Appendix D without changing.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Related Work section are unchanged. Section 4.2 adds a limited training-efficiency positioning argument, contrasting DART's 44,040,192 trainable parameters with CODI's 98,574,336 and Coconut's multistage full fine-tuning.

P1.justification: The empirical narrative is substantially reorganized: Appendix D is absorbed into Sections 4.2–4.3, alignment-token discussion joins the main ablations, and existing model-specific settings move to Appendix C. Section 4.3 becomes Further Analysis with task, model, and qualitative subsections. Most introductory, methodological, and related-work prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds resource and task-result tables, merges v1 Tables 2 and 6 into Table 3, moves Figure 2 into the main text, and transposes and expands the cross-model table. Dataset statistics and example boxes also expand. The framework diagram and sensitivity curves themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its reasoning claims only with arithmetic tasks and emphasizes inference efficiency. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence through logic and commonsense evaluations, a larger-model test, and quantified training costs. The resource table makes the trade-off more transparent, including DART's higher peak memory than CoT, 18.07 versus 12.28 GB. Original findings are preserved, although uncertainty reporting remains absent.
